To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the evolution characteristics of the BH in the Blandford–Znajek process and in the magnetic coupling process are studied in detail, the power dissipation on the black hole horizon and the black hole entropy increase are discussed, and the energy extracting efficiency is analyzed.
the BZ process is more effective than the MC process in energy extraction from the BH and the BH entropy increase is mainly due to the BZ process.
the BH energy extracting efficiency in the coexistence of BZ process and MC process is determined by the BH mass, the BH spin, the disc accretion rate and the magnetic field intensity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the energy evolution and BH entropy increase of the Kerr BH in the context of accretion disc theory, and provides a new method to study the energy evolution of BHs in the accretion disc.
the evolution characteristics of a magnetized BH, which may provide a new insight into the evolution of BHs in astrophysical environments.
the coexistence of accretion with energy extraction from a rotating BH in the context of magnetized accretions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the BZ and MC processes are the two important mechanisms for the energy extracting from the rotating BH and the BH evolution.
the BH evolution is determined by the competition of the BZ process, MC process and disc accretion.
the BH evolution in the coexistence of these energy extracting mechanisms is a complicated problem and should be investigated further.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a BH can be considered as a power station, which can convert the rotational energy into electromagnetic radiation.
the BH evolution characteristics and power dissipation on the horizon can be described in a unified way by using the characteristic function of the BH evolution.
the BH evolution is dominated by the BZ process in the case of low accretion rate and the MC process in the case for high accretion rate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the BH entropy is not only determined by its mass but also affected by the energy extracting process.
the BZ process is more efficient than the MC process in extracting energy from a rotating BH.
the BZ process is dominant in extracting energy from the BH when the BH is in the state of low accretion rate and high magnetic field.
